    // slot label name the same adult ("the second adult", etc.).
    _ ->
      "Upload an employer / business reference for "
      <> co_applicant_ordinal_from_key(key)
      <> "."

Nearest tests assert keys only (application_handler_test.gleam:864-868):

  errors
  |> list.any(fn(e) { e.0 == "employer_ref_coapplicant_0" })

evidence:
#text(font: "Geist", weight: 500, size: 10pt, fill: slate)[Employer / business reference]
...
#field-line("Employer / business reference", provided(app.documents.employer_ref))

Test assertions (audit_report_test.gleam:218-220):
      let assert Ok(pdf_bytes) = audit_report.generate(data, priv_dir())
      bit_array.byte_size(pdf_bytes) |> should.not_equal(0)
      bit_array.slice(pdf_bytes, 0, 5) |> should.equal(Ok(<<"%PDF-":utf8>>))
detail: maximal_snapshot() exercises both changed hunks (employment_status "employed", unconditional documents block), so template breakage fails — but assertions stop at non-empty %PDF- bytes. A label typo would compile and ship green; PDF text extraction is impractical at unit level.
